newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to invest T$350.9 bln in agriculture.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to invest T$350.9 bln in agriculture.

text.p: Taiwan planned to invest a total of T$350.9 billion over the next four years for development of agriculture, the Council of Agriculture said in a statement on Thursday.
The huge investment was aimed at maintaining "appropriate" agricultural growth, boosting agriculture value and farmers' income, the statement said.
Taiwan, eager to join the World Trade Organisation, has expected to encounter fundamental changes in its agriculture industry, but the government has vowed to protect the interests of farmers.
Although the statement did not directly mention the impact of WTO accession, it said the investment would help restructure the island's agriculture industry "to face the new situation".
The statement said the investment will be carried out under 158 projects, but did not elaborate.
Part of the funding will be used to subsidise farmers who will be asked to cut their sugar canes production as part of the government's compromise to join the world trade club.
Taiwan has said it planned to cut annual sugar production by about 160,000 tonnes to 310,000 tonnes by 2000.
To comply with international practice, the government would also reduce existing guaranteed prices for corn, soybeans and sorghum and subsidise part of farmers' losses with cash, the statement said.
Taiwan applied in 1990 to join GATT as a customs territory under the name of Chinese Taipei.
GATT was replaced by the WTO in January 1995.
Taiwan has made major concessions in recent years in its drive to join the world trade body, allowing more imports and opening up domestic markets and dismantling state monopolies.
Taiwan has said it wants to join the WTO in 1997.
